title: TIPS: Turn-level Information-Potential Reward Shaping for Search-Augmented LLMs
claim: Dense turn-level rewards from a teacher model, combined with a final outcome reward, replace sparse outcome-only feedback in multi-turn agent training.
layout: Left-to-right flow, 4 columns, conversation turns box feeding two parallel reward branches
description: A left-to-right flow diagram on a white background. On the far left, a blue robot icon labeled 'Policy model' exchanges arrows with a monitor-and-magnifier icon labeled 'Env'. A blue arrow leads into a tall rounded 'Conversation' box. It contains a green system prompt/user question block, then three black-outlined agent turns, each listing Reasoning, Query and Search results. The last turn ends in an orange 'Final answer'. Arrows lead from the turns to the right. A green robot labeled 'Teacher model' feeds a gold trophy for 'Information reward'. A clipboard icon labeled 'Answer verifier' feeds a trophy for 'Outcome reward'. An orange 'Ground truth' box links the teacher and the verifier. Both trophies point to a final 'TIPS reward' trophy at the right.
caption: Overview of our training framework. The policy model interacts with the environment by conducting multi-turn conversations: each turn consists of reasoning, issuing a query, and receiving search results, until a final answer is produced. Two dense reward signals are then derived: (i) an outcome reward, obtained by verifying whether the final answer matches the ground truth; and (ii) an information reward, provided by a teacher model that measures the information gain each turn contributes toward the ground truth. Both rewards are combined and optimized with PPO.
abstract: Search-augmented large language models (LLMs) trained with reinforcement learning (RL) have achieved strong results on open-domain question answering (QA), but training still remains a significant challenge. The optimization is often unstable due to sparse rewards and difficult credit assignments across reasoning and tool calls. To address this, we introduce Turn-Level Information Potential Reward Shaping (TIPS), a simple framework that assigns dense, turn-level rewards to each reasoning + tool-call segment based on the increased likelihood of the correct answer under a teacher model. By leveraging the potential-based reward shaping, TIPS offers fine-grained and policy-invariant guidance that overcomes the limitations of outcome-only optimization. Evaluated on seven QA benchmarks, TIPS consistently outperforms GRPO/PPO baselines and substantially improves training stability. For instance, with a Qwen-2.5 7B Instruct model, TIPS improves the average Exact Match score by 11.8% and F1 by 13.6% relative to PPO. Our results demonstrate that turn-level information-potential reward shaping provides an effective and general solution to sparse-reward credit assignment for multi-turn LLM reasoning.
